extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and microbial/pathogenesis researchers (PIs, postdocs, grad students, collaborators)
extracted.subtask_description: An NIH-style Research Strategy section describing aims, preliminary data, experimental design, expected outcomes, contingencies, timeline, biosafety, and training for a microbiology project (Coxiella burnetii; heme biosynthesis and HGT-focused).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of transposon-insertion mutants for functional validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize transposon-insertion (Tn) mutants — specifically strains with insertions causing only partial loss-of-function when full loss would be lethal — to validate the utility of metabolic pathways for intracellular growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search available Tn-insertion libraries (collaborators cited) to identify partial-loss alleles; example given: Tn insertion in the 3' end of hemL reduced intracellular growth (Figure 8). Anti-pattern: using only null insertions for essential genes (likely lethal) without alternative partial-loss strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of horizontally derived genes (HGT detection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify most horizontally derived genes in C. burnetii as a primary expected outcome for understanding its evolution from a tick-associated ancestor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply comparative genomics and phylogenetic analyses; leverage existing databases and collaborators with phylogenetic expertise. Expectation: a comprehensive catalog of HGT-acquired genes that can inform downstream prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize metabolic pathways containing horizontally acquired genes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize metabolic pathways for validation when they contain foreign-origin (HGT) genes maintained in Coxiella’s reduced genome, because maintenance implies likely contribution to organismal fitness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: heme and fatty acid biosynthesis pathways. Prioritization rationale: retention in streamlined genome and expression during intracellular growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation by combining gene expression and mutant phenotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate importance of pathogen-specific and HGT-containing pathways by analyzing gene expression and assessing Tn-insertion or deletion mutant phenotypes on intracellular growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare expression in ACCM-2 versus infected THP-1 cells to identify host-induced genes; use both RNA-seq data and mutant growth assays to corroborate functional importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathway-validation prioritization criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize pathways for validation using these ordered criteria: (1) synthesis of metabolites C. burnetii cannot obtain from host (e.g., heme, biotin), (2) pathways for metabolizing critical nutrients (e.g., glutamate), (3) proteins required for homeostasis (e.g., Na+/H+ antiporters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metabolic necessity and host-independence as primary filters when choosing targets for genetic validation and chemical screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include student training and explicit roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe trainee involvement (graduate and undergraduate students) and assign concrete responsibilities tied to Aims and experiments as an expected outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names/roles and evidence of prior trainee competence; link training tasks to specific methods (e.g., RNA-seq analysis, Tn mutant analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate potential problems and provide alternative strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly list potential impediments for each aim and describe alternate strategies or backups to overcome them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sparse phylogenetic representation → collaborate with phylogeny expert; low bacterial mRNA from THP-1 → sequence without multiplexing; differences between phase I and II strains → obtain phase I RNA from BSL-3 collaborator; heme assay inconsistency → alternate assay or commercial kit. Good proposals include specific fallbacks rather than vague assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target selection rationale (uniqueness, HGT, expression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select targets (e.g., heme biosynthesis) based on threefold rationale: unique to human pathogen, contains horizontally derived genes, and is expressed during intracellular growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use genomic presence/absence across related species and RNA-seq expression data within host cells to justify target choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple, independent preliminary lines of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Support hypotheses with convergent preliminary data types: genomic analyses, expression (RNA-seq), chemical inhibition (gabaculine), transposon insertion effects, and targeted deletions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example outcomes: gabaculine inhibited growth (in vitro), hemL Tn insertion reduced growth, tRNAGlu2 deletion strain shows growth defect. Strong proposals use diverse preliminary evidence to justify feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementation to confirm causality
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct complementation strains (reintroduction of deleted gene/tRNA) to confirm that observed mutant phenotypes are due to the targeted deletion and not off-target changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan genetic complementation into a neutral intergenic site using established transposon/plasmid systems and collaborative expertise. Expect phenotype restoration as validation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative, validated assays for biochemical and growth readouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use established, quantitative assays to measure heme content and intracellular growth, with clear protocols and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heme: oxalic acid heating method with fluorescence measurement (Hughes & Macvanin 2010) and alternative absorbance-based method (Levican et al. 2007) or commercial kit. Growth: qPCR targeting rpoS and dotA, fluorescence microscopy using mCherry-expressing strains and vacuole enumeration. Include sample processing steps and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate controls, replication, and statistical testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Include biological/technical replicates and appropriate statistical tests (examples use paired t-tests with reported p-values and n), and present quantitative comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in preliminary data: PicoGreen growth assay p < 0.001 (paired t-test, n=4). Plan for sufficient sample sizes and report statistics for key comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage published methods and collaborators/letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite published protocols and identify collaborators who provide strains, BSL-3 access, plasmids, or methodological expertise (letters of support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: collaboration with Dr. Bonazzi and Dr. Samuel for Tn libraries; Dr. Paul Beare for genetic system; Dr. James Samuel for phase I RNA. Use collaborator-provided resources to mitigate technical gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a realistic research timeline with milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Map specific tasks/assays to months/years and show how aims are phased across the project duration (three-year timeline provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example timeline: genome assembly (9 months), annotation (3 months), comparative genomics (3 months), phylogenetics (12 months), RNA-seq (6 months), Tn analyses (6 months), complementation (6 months), heme measurement (3 months), growth measurement (3 months). Use Gantt-style mapping to demonstrate feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select-agent and biosafety compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state select-agent status and containment level; use avirulent/exempt strains and approved genetic markers per regulatory approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Coxiella burnetii Category B Select Agent — work uses avirulent, exempt Nine Mile Phase II strain (RSA 439) under BSL-2. Note that kanamycin and chloramphenicol resistance markers are approved for Coxiella genetic transformation by CDC Select Agents Program. Plans must adhere to institutional and federal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for downstream translational follow-up (chemical screens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include next-step plans to identify small molecules inhibiting validated metabolic targets, leveraging translational screening collaborations and student involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: screen small-molecule libraries for inhibitors of heme or biotin biosynthesis (MAC13772 example), collaborate with translational research institute (OTRADI). This demonstrates broader impact and future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of proteomics and omics resources for negative/complex phenotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: If genetic deletions do not produce clear phenotypes, use proteomics (MS/MS) to identify impacted proteins and infer affected metabolic processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sample prep (SDS-PAGE, trypsin digestion), instrument (LTQ mass spectrometer), database searching (Proteome Software Scaffold), and core facility support. Have alternative plans to interpret null genetic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require phenotype restoration in complementation as validation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect both biochemical (heme production) and phenotypic (intracellular growth) defects in deletion strains to be significantly lower than wild-type and restored in complementation strains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State this as an explicit validation criterion: decreased heme and growth in deletion strain and recovery in complemented strain will validate target importance and causal link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure sufficient sequencing depth for RNA-seq
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust library multiplexing or sequencing strategy to obtain adequate bacterial mRNA coverage, especially when intracellular bacterial load is low (e.g., in THP-1 cells).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bacterial mRNA yield is low, sequence without multiplexing to increase read depth. Plan per-sample sequencing depth to enable reliable gene expression quantification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare gene expression across biologically relevant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify genes induced within host cells by comparing expression profiles between axenic medium (ACCM-2) and infected host cells (THP-1 or Vero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RNA-seq to detect host-induced genes and prioritize those highly expressed intracellularly for functional validation; tie expression patterns to functional hypotheses (e.g., tRNAGlu2 expression high intracellularly suggests role in heme biosynthesis).
